purpose: Read-only inspection of three native Microsoft Word bidi and East Asian language fixtures, including OOXML language and font associations, legacy DOC character-format runs, and native RTF controls.

provenance.authoring_method: Computer Use / native Microsoft Word UI
provenance.source: Seven paragraphs were entered in native Word. The Arabic, Hebrew, Japanese, and Chinese paragraph language settings were selected through Tools > Language. The font dialog was used with Arial for Arabic and Hebrew, Hiragino Mincho ProN for Japanese, and Songti SC for Chinese. Native Word saved the DOCX, DOC, and RTF files; each file was closed and reopened without a repair prompt before final closure.

coverage.feature: native language selection and script text
coverage.evidence: All three files preserve the seven exact marker paragraphs. DOCX records direct he-IL, ja-JP, and zh-CN language properties and inherits Arabic bidi language ar-SA from docDefaults; DOC and RTF preserve corresponding language IDs and script-specific controls.

coverage.feature: Latin, complex-script, and East Asian font associations
coverage.evidence: DOCX records Arial Black for Latin prefixes/spaces, Arial plus cs=Arial for Arabic/Hebrew words, Hiragino Mincho ProN W3 for Japanese, Songti SC Light for Chinese, and fallback cs fonts MS Gothic/Microsoft JhengHei. The DOC FFN table and CHP runs carry the same native font choices.

litchi-docx reads seven paragraphs and zero tables with exact Unicode text, but its document text projection concatenates paragraph text without paragraph separators and does not expose the language/font properties in this example.

litchi-doc reads seven paragraphs and zero tables, preserves 246 characters including paragraph separators, and exposes native CHP font indexes, language IDs, and FarEast script hints through Run properties.
litchi-rtf exits with MalformedDocument("RTF data-store payload cannot be empty") at the native empty starred datastore group. textutil still extracts the exact seven-line text.

DOCX has zero w:bidi and w:rtl elements, RTF has zero \rtlpar controls and two \ltrpar controls, and the tested Word UI did not expose a separate paragraph direction setting. Character-level complex-script controls must not be treated as paragraph direction.

The Japanese text intentionally contains punctuation and brackets, but DOCX has no w:kinsoku, settings.xml has no w:kinsoku, and the native UI path exposed no Asian Typography/Kinsoku control. RTF contains asianbrkrule but no kinsoku control; this is raw compatibility evidence only.

facts: Arabic paragraph index 2 uses Arial Black for its Latin prefix and spaces and Arial/cs=Arial for Arabic runs.
Hebrew paragraph index 3 carries direct w:lang bidi=he-IL on its paragraph properties and nine runs.
Japanese paragraph index 4 carries eastAsia=ja-JP and Hiragino Mincho ProN W3 with cs=MS Gothic on the body run.
Chinese paragraph index 5 carries eastAsia=zh-CN and Songti SC Light with alternating cs=MS Gothic and Microsoft JhengHei.
There are no w:bidi, w:rtl, or w:kinsoku elements.
docDefaults w:lang is en-US/eastAsia=en-US/bidi=ar-SA; the Arabic paragraph has no direct w:lang bidi attribute.
No w:bidi, w:rtl, or w:kinsoku setting is present; only ordinary compatibility and theme language settings are present.
The package font table contains nine native entries including Arial Black, Arial, Hiragino Mincho ProN W3, MS Gothic, Songti SC Light, and Microsoft JhengHei.
The raw RTF contains script-specific font IDs, associated-font controls, language controls, Unicode controls, and one empty starred datastore destination; it has no rtlpar or kinsoku control.
The typed RTF parser rejects a starred datastore destination when its hexadecimal payload is empty.

known_limits: The Arabic OOXML language is inherited from styles.xml docDefaults bidi=ar-SA; this fixture does not evidence a direct Arabic w:lang bidi attribute.

The native Word UI path did not expose an explicit RTL paragraph direction or Asian Kinsoku control. Character-level rtlch/fcs/af controls in RTF and cs/font associations in OOXML must not be reported as paragraph direction or proof of Kinsoku processing.
The DOCX example reader exposes text and paragraph/table counts but not OOXML language or font properties; raw package inspection and the legacy DOC Run properties provide the format evidence.
The RTF typed reader stops at the empty datastore before it can provide parsed font or run objects; all RTF font, language, and compatibility facts above are raw-source observations.

native_ui_follow_up_candidates.minimal_action: Duplicate the native fixture, select only the Arabic paragraph, choose Tools > Language > Arabic, save a fresh DOCX, and compare document.xml/styles.xml.
native_ui_follow_up_candidates.discriminator: A direct w:lang bidi value on the Arabic paragraph would distinguish direct selection from the current docDefaults bidi=ar-SA inheritance.

native_ui_follow_up_candidates.minimal_action: In a duplicate native fixture, use any available Home/Paragraph right-to-left command on only the Hebrew paragraph, save DOCX and RTF, and inspect for w:bidi or rtlpar.
native_ui_follow_up_candidates.discriminator: A newly emitted w:bidi or \rtlpar would be direct paragraph-direction evidence; the current fixture has neither.

native_ui_follow_up_candidates.minimal_action: In a duplicate native fixture, expose Word's Asian Typography/line-break settings if available for the Japanese paragraph, toggle one setting, save DOCX and RTF, and compare package/settings controls.
native_ui_follow_up_candidates.discriminator: A w:kinsoku or RTF kinsoku control would distinguish a real setting from punctuation text alone; no such control is present currently.

native_ui_follow_up_candidates.minimal_action: Save a fresh one-paragraph native Word RTF with no script formatting and compare its root starred destinations with this file, retaining the current empty-datastore group as the boundary candidate.
native_ui_follow_up_candidates.discriminator: If the fresh native RTF also has {\*\datastore } and litchi-rtf returns the same error, the failure is producer-wide rather than bidi/East Asian-specific.
